title: A longitudinal analysis to differentiate viral and bacterial infections using the diagnostic and prognostic value of Arg9-Bradykinine for pneumonia.
summary:
What is pneumonia?

Pneumonia is a common infectious disease that affects many people worldwide. It can be particularly dangerous for patients who are being treated in hospital or in intensive care. Doctors need to find out whether the pneumonia is caused by bacteria or viruses, as this determines which treatment – such as antibiotics – is necessary.

What are the pathogens?

In Germany, bacterial pneumonia is more common in adults than viral pneumonia. The most common bacterial pathogen is Streptococcus pneumoniae, which causes what is known as community-acquired pneumonia (CAP). Other bacteria such as Haemophilus influenzae or Legionella may also be involved. Viral pneumonia is often caused by influenza viruses, RSV, or the coronavirus (SARS-CoV-2), especially during certain times of the year. In hospitals, so-called nosocomial pneumonia (HAP) can be caused by resistant bacteria such as Pseudomonas aeruginosa or Staphylococcus aureus.

Why is diagnosis difficult?

Doctors use tests such as C-reactive protein (CRP) or procalcitonin (PCT) to detect pneumonia and assess its severity. However, these tests do not always clearly indicate whether bacteria or viruses are the cause. This can lead to unnecessary use of antibiotics or delays in the right treatment.

What is Des-Arg9-Bradykinin (DABK)?

DABK is a substance in the body that plays an important role in pneumonia. It is produced when a certain enzyme (ACE2) does not function properly, which is common in severe respiratory diseases. DABK influences how permeable blood vessels are and how many immune cells (especially neutrophils) enter the lungs. In bacterial pneumonia, this often leads to severe inflammation, while viral pneumonia tends to cause fluid in the lungs (pulmonary edema). Studies show that higher DABK levels are associated with more severe disease progression and problems such as circulatory failure or vascular damage.

What does the study aim to find out?

The study is investigating whether DABK can help doctors better determine whether pneumonia is caused by bacteria or viruses. It will also examine whether DABK can indicate how severe the disease is likely to be. To do this, DABK levels will be measured over time and compared with other measurements. In addition, the study will investigate whether other substances in the blood can further improve the diagnosis.

Why is this important?

If DABK works as a reliable marker, doctors could choose the right treatment more quickly and better predict severe cases. This would make the treatment of pneumonia more precise and effective.

interventions.name: Adults (≥18 years) requiring intensive care with suspected pneumonia. Biomarker analysis of serum Arg9-Bradykinine will be collected at 4 different time points to determine the time course of Arg9-Bradykinine in pneumonia of different etiologies in Intesive Care Patients. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Adults (≥18 years) requiring intensive care with suspected pneumonia
Exclusion criteria:
Patients with pre-existing pneumonia (longer than 24 hours) at the time of admission/onset of illness.
Patients with pre-existing chronic autoimmune disease (e.g., Crohn's disease, rheumatoid arthritis) at the time of admission/onset of illness.
